In 50 periodontal surgery patients, binaural-beat exposure was associated with lower postoperative anxiety and physiological stress measures than no auditory intervention. Mean anxiety scores in the intervention arm fell from 49.0 to 38.7.

Preoperative binaural-beat stimulation produced a greater reduction in reported state anxiety than the control condition. The reported difference in relative anxiety change was approximately six percentage points.

A pilot involving 30 people with multiple sclerosis and 30 healthy participants reported lower salivary cortisol after 4 Hz binaural stimulation than sham following an experimental stress challenge, alongside autonomic and EEG changes.
In 96 patients undergoing unsedated upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, binaural-beat music was associated with improved anxiety, procedure tolerance and satisfaction compared with no intervention.
A 61-person cataract-surgery trial reported lower operative pain, anxiety and heart rate with binaural-beat audio than with silent headphones.

Among 64 older adults with poor sleep in long-term care, binaural beats embedded in familiar music improved sleep measures and selected autonomic measures relative to the same music without beats over 14 days.
In 99 root-canal patients, binaural beats and 432 Hz music each reduced preoperative anxiety relative to white noise. Participants and outcome assessors were described as blinded.
Among 112 bronchoscopy patients, the binaural-music arm showed a larger numerical reduction in state anxiety than plain music or no music, with reductions in blood pressure.
A 252-child dental trial reported reduced preoperative fear, anxiety and physiological arousal with device-based brainwave entrainment compared with standard behaviour management.
Among 27 stroke rehabilitation completers, the binaural-stimulation group improved daily-living and depression scores more than the music comparison group. Balance measures improved in both groups.

Of 151 women randomised after a traumatic birth, 143 entered the reported intention-to-treat analysis. Two early postpartum EMDR sessions reduced self-reported and clinician-rated PTSD symptom severity compared with two telephone contacts; the reported raw symptom differences were 8.7 and 3.8 points respectively.

In 159 people with personality disorders, EMDR reduced PTSD symptoms more than a waitlist. Among participants with PTSD receiving EMDR, 65.5% no longer met the diagnosis after treatment and 73.1% at follow-up.

In 24 forensic patients with psychosis and PTSD, blinded assessments favoured EMDR over routine-care waitlist for clinician-rated PTSD symptoms. The estimated difference averaged across follow-ups was 11.4 points, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.3 to 21.4.

In 120 women exposed to violence, ten sessions of EMDR produced greater reported improvements in post-traumatic symptoms, anxiety, depression, quality of life and selected cognitive tests than narrative exposure therapy.

The 40-person EMERALD trial in critical-illness survivors achieved 98% clinician-rated follow-up at 12 months. Exploratory PTSD symptom change favoured EMDR plus usual care by 14.1 points, with a 95% confidence interval of 6.2 to 22.0 points.

A 38-person pilot found greater reductions in binge-eating symptoms, days and frequency with an adapted ten-session EMDR protocol than waitlist, alongside improvements in selected anxiety and sleep outcomes.

In 60 early-psychosis service users, a 16-session EMDR adaptation met trial feasibility targets and showed promising clinical signals at six months. PTSD symptoms and general-health signals remained evident at 12 months.

In 22 treatment-resistant depression inpatients, both EMDR and trauma-focused CBT improved depressive symptoms; a post-hoc comparison favoured EMDR at the 12-week follow-up.
In 20 people with bipolar disorder and trauma histories, EMDR improved depressive, hypomanic and trauma symptoms relative to usual care after treatment, using blinded outcome ratings.
In 20 people with bipolar disorder and trauma histories, EMDR improved depressive, hypomanic and trauma symptoms relative to usual care after treatment, using blinded outcome ratings.
A 155-person international trial found substantial PTSD improvement after either EMDR or imagery rescripting for childhood-related trauma, with a 7.7% dropout rate.
In 140 people with PTSD, EMDR and brief eclectic psychotherapy produced similar final improvements; EMDR achieved improvement more rapidly during treatment.
Among 114 participants in the IREM childhood-trauma trial, both EMDR and imagery rescripting improved adaptive and maladaptive schema-mode measures, with gains maintained to one year.

An eight-week workplace mindfulness study, with 25 meditators and 16 waitlist participants tested, reported greater left-anterior EEG activation and a stronger influenza-vaccine antibody response in the meditation group.

Among 90 cancer outpatients completing a seven-week mindfulness programme, mood disturbance and stress symptoms improved relative to waitlist; the intervention group reported reductions of 65% and 31% respectively.
In 84 breast-cancer survivors, six weeks of adapted MBSR improved depression, anxiety, fear of recurrence and selected quality-of-life measures relative to usual care.

In 49 older adults with sleep disturbance, mindful-awareness training improved Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores by 1.8 points more than structured sleep-hygiene education, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.6 to 2.9.
In a 93-person generalised-anxiety trial, MBSR improved several secondary anxiety ratings and stress-challenge responses more than stress-management education.
In 150 people with multiple sclerosis, eight weeks of mindfulness training improved nonphysical quality of life, depression and fatigue relative to usual care, with benefits persisting at six months.
In an 88-person smoking-cessation trial, mindfulness training reduced smoking more than the comparison programme; carbon-monoxide-confirmed seven-day abstinence at week 17 was 31% versus 6%.

In the 616-student Mindful Student Study, an eight-week course reduced exam-period psychological distress relative to usual support. The adjusted difference was -0.14 CORE-OM points, with a 95% confidence interval of -0.22 to -0.06.

In 286 adults completing substance-use treatment, mindfulness-based relapse prevention reduced substance-use days and heavy drinking at 12 months relative to standard relapse prevention and usual aftercare.
In a 73-person recurrent-depression trial, MBCT reduced relapse among the 55 participants with three or more prior episodes: 36% relapsed versus 78% with usual care.

A two-site trial in 173 veterans found greater clinician-rated PTSD improvement with an eight-week mantram programme than present-centred therapy; the between-group CAPS difference was approximately ten points. Insomnia also improved.
A small mantram study in combat veterans reported promising effects on PTSD symptoms, distress and quality of life, with 29 of 33 enrolled participants completing the study.

In a 146-veteran trial, adding mantram repetition to usual care increased mindful attention; changes in mindful attention statistically mediated improvements in PTSD symptoms, depression and wellbeing.
In the 173-veteran mantram trial, hyperarousal improved more than with nonspecific psychotherapy, with effect sizes of 0.57 after treatment and 0.52 at follow-up.
A 26-person internet mantram pilot in breast-cancer survivors established delivery feasibility and reported exploratory changes in stress, spiritual wellbeing and selected serum cytokines.
In 22 veterans receiving MBSR, responders showed increased FKBP5 methylation while nonresponders showed decreased methylation, following the corrected direction reported in the 2021 corrigendum.

In 40 veterans with PTSD, Transcendental Meditation reduced clinician-rated symptoms more than usual care over 12 weeks. Half of the meditation group no longer met PTSD criteria, compared with 10% of controls.
In 181 male prisoners, Transcendental Meditation reduced self-reported trauma symptoms and perceived stress relative to usual care after four months.
A 104-nurse trial across three hospitals reported improved wellbeing and lower burnout, anxiety and PTSD symptoms after Transcendental Meditation compared with delayed instruction.
In 199 women living in poverty in Uganda, three months of Transcendental Meditation reduced perceived stress, anger and fatigue and improved self-efficacy and sleep quality relative to waitlist.
In 114 rural Lebanese women, three months of Transcendental Meditation improved stress, happiness, resilience and self-efficacy relative to the comparison group.

In 96 school-district staff, Transcendental Meditation improved mood and distress relative to waitlist over four months. An EEG subset of 79 participants also showed changes in the study's Brain Integration Scale.

In 2,182 NHS staff, a digital mindfulness app produced a small but statistically significant reduction in stress relative to an active digital control over 4.5 months, with additional benefits on several wellbeing measures.
In 1,458 employees, an eight-week digital meditation programme improved perceived stress relative to waitlist, with an effect size of 0.85 at eight weeks and 0.71 at four months.

In 1,281 adults with substantial psychological distress, an eight-week hybrid digital mindfulness programme plus usual services reduced distress more than usual services alone, with an effect size of approximately 0.53.
